intro: Text to STL creates 3D letters from what you type: signs, name plates, labels for boxes and shelves, cake toppers, signage or personalised gifts. There is no file to upload: type the text, choose the font and download the STL.

You can type several lines and align them left, centre or right. Six fonts are included, from the DejaVu family (sans, serif, monospace and condensed, regular or bold), with accents, ñ and most European symbols. The size is the capital letter height in millimetres.

Choose the letter thickness and, if you want, a base plate with a margin under the text: that gives a one-piece sign with raised letters. Letters that touch are merged into a single closed solid, with no internal faces.
Up to 300 characters per text. The result comes out as STL, 3MF or OBJ and is created in an isolated process on our server in the European Union; it is deleted when it expires.
steps: Choose the font, size and thickness.

faq.q: Can I use my own font?
faq.a: Not yet: the six included DejaVu fonts, with a free licence, are used.

faq.q: Do the letters come out stuck together?
faq.a: Only if they touch in the font's design; with a base plate, everything comes out in one piece.
For a door sign, about 20 mm capitals; for a small label, 6 to 8 mm.
Yes: type the name, enable the base plate and then drill the hole or add it in your slicer.

faq.q: Does it support accents and symbols?
faq.a: Yes: DejaVu covers accents, ñ, ç, the euro sign and most European symbols.
